newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS-KL stocks roiled anew by Dow, ringgit drop.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-KL stocks roiled anew by Dow, ringgit drop.

text.p: Malaysia's share market tumbled on Monday after Wall Street's big slide on Friday and the ringgit continued to weaken against the dollar, dealers and analysts said.

The benchmark Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index of 100 top companies closed 29.73 points, or 3.27 percent, lower at 880.45. It hit an intraday low of 877.47, its weakest level since January 27, 1995, when it touched 836.93.

Blue-chip stocks were among the hardest hit. On Friday, the Dow Jones industrial average posted its second-largest point loss, falling 247.37 points, or 3.11 percent to 7,694.66, due to a weak U.S. dollar and worries over U.S. corporate results.
"These two factors have definitely been the main reasons for the fall on the (Composite) index today," said a vice president of stock index futures trading at a local brokerage firm.
"People are expecting the ringgit to fall further. That's what's further dampening the market," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage.
"If anything worse could have happened, it happened last Friday when the Dow Jones fell..." said Jupiter Securities in a daily market report.
The Malaysian currency weakened further on Monday. At 0800 GMT the ringgit stood at 2.7900 against the U.S. dollar. It had closed in Kuala Lumpur on Friday at 2.7780.
During Friday's trading it broke above the 2.80 level to its weakest levels since it was first floated in 1973.

Adding to the gloom, U.S. rating agency Standard & Poor's Corp (S&P) said on Monday it had revised the outlook on Malaysia's long-term A-plus foreign currency and AA-plus local currency ratings to stable from positive.
S&P also said it had affirmed Malaysia's A1-plus short-term rating.
Analysts said the move did not significantly affect share prices on Monday.
Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad continued to reject criticism that Malaysia's economy is overheating, saying on Monday his country needs to develop faster.

"We have to move fast and run faster. If we were to run slower, we will never catch up and the gap would be even greater and forever we will be left behind," said Mahathir in a speech in Sarawak state on Borneo island.
Mahathir and Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim have said that certain infrastructure projects may have to be deferred to reduce the burden on the country's current account deficit.
Malaysia's largest bank Malayan Banking Bhd, telecommunications and power utilities Telekom Malaysia Bhd and Tenaga Nasional Bhd lost between 35 cents ($0.125) and one ringgit.
Conglomerate Sime Darby Bhd lost 20 cents to 7.70 ringgit.
Together the issues comprise 33 percent of the weighting of the Composite Index.
Analysts said the next support level for the index appeared to be between 830 and 850.
"I don't think there are any more major sellers. I expect the market to consolidate around the 880 level," said Ken Loo, head of research at Amsteel Securities.
($1=2.79 ringgit)
